subject: health
unitTitle: Mental Health Maintenance and Sustainable Coping
title: Explicit model: maintenance strategies versus emergency strategies
essentialQuestion: How do I keep myself steady through a transition that removes most of my structure?
privacySafeScenario: Write a transition plan with maintenance strategies, early-warning conditions the learner will watch for, and a concrete first step for getting professional support — including how it would be paid for and accessed.
studentTask: Learner applies maintenance strategies versus emergency strategies to a new fictional scenario and records the response with the reasoning, evidence, or decision process behind it.
knowledgeCheck: In one concise response, show or explain the most important idea about maintenance strategies versus emergency strategies, then name one check that would catch a weak claim or an unsafe step.
completionCriteria: The learner completes the central task about maintenance strategies versus emergency strategies without being asked for any private disclosure.
The learner gives evidence, reasoning, a documented process, or a cited source rather than an unsupported claim.
The learner checks or revises the work and can identify a next step.
adaptationChoices: The plan may be written, spoken, or assembled from supplied strategy cards. General categories may be used throughout instead of specific personal detail.
extensionChallenge: Apply maintenance strategies versus emergency strategies under a new constraint, compare two approaches, or explain the idea to someone else with an original fictional example, without completing another learner's graded work.
